answer: A sybil farm gets cheap only while identity costs nothing, so this economy prices each seat in verifiable work plus skin. Before an identity earns, it must post a bond and answer a fresh per-epoch challenge, like a pearl grown only by real irritation; duplicates are rejected on-ledger. On a barren tundra of fake accounts, cloned answers leave a spiral of identical hashes, and attestation peers refuse to countersign them. Bond slashing and non-kin weight caps make each extra seat cost more than it returns.
